findings.finding: No natural contract repair was exercised
findings.detail: All 32 stages passed their first normal unittest invocation. There were 33 invocations in total, all passing. Both conditions produced 16/16 complete final artifacts. This cohort does not establish an incremental checker effect or demonstrate a failing contract corrected from test feedback.

findings.finding: Checker source can be read as guidance before testing
findings.detail: Claude checker read source before component creation in 6/8 stages, after creation in revise, and had no separate source read in revised_direct. Codex checker read source before creation in 8/8. Source delivery and final success are correlated observations, not evidence that the read caused correct code.

findings.finding: Shell recovery is distinct from checker repair
findings.detail: Codex baseline historical first passed 36 tests after a here-document failed to create replay tests, then added its replay test file and passed 41 tests. The component was not changed between these successful runs. Other here-document errors occurred during memory/task authoring. None was a public contract failure.

findings.finding: Incomplete exact field retention can coexist with correct work
findings.detail: Claude checker retained the correct v1 policy, rationale, approval ID, date and separate version marker, but omitted ", version v1" from the exact SOURCE phrase. The same body was copied verbatim to catalog-api.response-cache.v1-snapshot during revision. Thus the exact-source omission persisted, without loss of factual source identity. Earlier correct component source remained available and was read; full artifact success does not certify memory-only fidelity.

findings.finding: Full bodies can be returned by JSON search
findings.detail: Claude checker historical recovered the entire v1 note through bd memories "v1-snapshot" --json after attempted memories list/show commands. It made no explicit bd recall call. This is full-body retrieval via query output, distinct from both previews and the prescribed explicit recall route.

Independent trace and memory-map inspection found three actual memory writes per lifecycle: retain current v1, retain original snapshot, and revise current to v2. All reproduction stages preserved memory bodies with no writes. Baseline Claude described its original snapshot as an immutable record; interpret this as requested preservation, not a legacy CLI enforcement guarantee. No other material unsupported provenance or historical claims were found.

All actual authored follow-up tasks cite retained keys and applicability. Some also include policy values or richer component instructions. Both earlier tasks and code remain valid alternate sources. Identical harness-authored tasks do not imply identical agent-authored handoffs.

Claude baseline added component tests in all eight stages; Claude checker added them only in revised_search, supplied and historical. Both Codex conditions added tests in every stage. Hidden behavior grades pass throughout; these work-pattern differences do not prove a causal effect or a testing-quality ranking.

Codex checker establish streamed command output omits earlier cat outputs from the same command. Saved rollout line 36 contains the full checker source in the actual custom-tool result, before first patch at line 42. Exposure is verified via that result, not inferred solely from a requested cat command.
